metadata.project_title: Supervised Learning Based Approach for Mining ABAC Rules from Existing RBAC Enabled Systems
metadata.authoritative_source: Project report PDF (research methodology, Appendix B algorithm, evaluation metrics, scope)
metadata.note: This file is a governance specification read by humans and AI coding agents. It cannot enforce itself. Enforcement requires GitHub branch protection, CODEOWNERS, pull-request review and CI (see git_workflow.enforcement).

objective.summary: Build a working prototype that mines human-readable ABAC rules from an existing RBAC system using supervised machine learning.
pipeline_steps: Import RBAC data and user/resource attributes
Construct the RBAC authorisation relation Auth from UA and PA
Generate positive samples S+ and sampled negative samples S-
Train Decision Tree, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting; cross-validate and compare
Select the interpretable Decision Tree for rule extraction
Extract permit paths as candidate ABAC rules with support and confidence
Validate the policy against the full RBAC access matrix
Administrator reviews, approves, rejects or edits rules
Export approved rules as JSON and XACML-style policy
out_of_scope: Integration with a live policy decision point or production IAM
Environmental or contextual attributes (time, location, device)
Deny-rule mining as a mandatory feature

permission_levels.OWNER: Responsible for implementing and maintaining the module. May change it through the normal pull-request flow.
permission_levels.CONTRIBUTOR: May contribute only through an approved change request and a pull request reviewed by the OWNER.
permission_levels.READ_ONLY: May inspect, import and call the module but must not change it.
permission_levels.RESTRICTED: Any change needs explicit approval from the module OWNER and the project lead, recorded in the pull request.

team.decision_model: Technical integration is led by Jayed. Project-level decisions are shared among all four members. Jayed is not responsible for fixing other members' code.

jayed.designation: Machine Learning Engineer and Backend Lead

shweta.designation: Data Engineering and Quality Assurance Engineer

granthali.designation: Security Logic and ABAC Policy Engineer

backend_app.description: FastAPI application entry point, routers wiring, configuration

backend_api.description: REST route handlers. Response structures follow shared/schemas/contracts.py

backend_services.description: Orchestration layer connecting data pipeline, ML engine and policy engine

backend_data_pipeline.description: RBAC loading, preprocessing, authorisation matrix, positive/negative sample generation, encoding

backend_ml_engine.description: Model training, cross-validation, tuning, evaluation, decision tree permit-path extraction

backend_models.description: Serialised trained models (not committed to git)

backend_schemas.description: Backend-internal helpers that re-export or wrap shared contracts. Must not redefine contract models.

backend_utils.description: Backend utilities (logging, seeds, timing, config loading)

data_engineering.description: Sample datasets, data validation, test scenarios, data documentation

integration_tests.description: Cross-module tests: data validation, dataset generation, API, integration, end-to-end

policy_engine.description: ABAC rule schema, merging, generalisation, pruning, support/confidence, validation, WSC, JSON/XACML export, RBAC authorisation verification

shared_schemas.description: Single source of truth for data and API contracts (Pydantic)
shared_schemas.change_rule: Any change requires a contract change request approved by all four members and a CONTRACT_VERSION bump.

shared_sample_responses.description: Mock JSON responses used by the frontend and by tests. Must validate against shared_schemas.
shared_sample_responses.change_rule: Regenerate only through a contract change; mocks must validate against contracts.py.

docs.description: Architecture, module docs, team guides, development rules
docs.change_rule: Members may edit their own guide's progress sections and the module doc for their own module via pull request. Other docs need the OWNER's review.

governance_root.path: PROJECT_RULES.json, AGENTS.md, README.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md, ROADMAP.md, .github/, scripts/, .gitignore, requirements-base.txt, requirements-dev.txt
governance_root.change_rule: Changes need approval from all four members because they affect everyone.

config.description: Shared configuration (thresholds, seeds, paths). No secrets.
config.change_rule: Granthali may propose policy_engine-related keys through pull request reviewed by Jayed.

jayed_to_granthali.description: Jayed passes extracted candidate rules and the labelled samples to policy_engine through a Python function. policy_engine never imports from backend.
inputs: pandas DataFrame of encoded or decoded samples with a label column

jayed_to_granthali_validation.description: Final validation against the full access matrix

jayed_to_granthali_export.constraint: Only rules with status=approved may be exported.

shweta_to_all.description: Shweta provides sample datasets and validation functions. Jayed's loader may call data_engineering.data_validation as a library; data_engineering must remain importable without the backend.

frontend_to_backend.description: REST over JSON. Base URL from environment variable VITE_API_BASE_URL. Mock mode via VITE_USE_MOCKS=true loading shared/sample_responses.

naming_conventions.ids: dataset_id: ds_NNN, run_id: run_NNN, policy_id: pol_NNN, rule_id: RNNN, model_id: m_<type>_NNN

python.typing: Type hints on all public functions
python.docstrings: Every public function and class has a docstring stating inputs, outputs and failure behaviour
python.randomness: Every stochastic step accepts random_seed; default 42; never rely on global random state
python.errors: Raise explicit exceptions with clear messages; never swallow exceptions silently

javascript.style: ESLint defaults for React; functional components and hooks only
javascript.api_access: All HTTP calls go through frontend/src/services/ only; components never call fetch directly

general: No dead code or commented-out blocks in pull requests
No hardcoded file system paths; use config/
No duplicate implementation of existing functionality

api_standards.format: JSON request and response (multipart/form-data for uploads)
api_standards.success_envelope: Every success body has status: ok
api_standards.error_envelope: ErrorResponse from shared/schemas/contracts.py with a non-2xx HTTP status

status_codes.409: invalid state transition (for example export before approval)
status_codes.500: unexpected server error (never returns a permit)

api_standards.versioning: Breaking changes require a new path version and approval from all members

data_standards.encoding: UTF-8, header row required, snake_case column names
data_standards.missing_values: Reported by validation as warnings; imputation strategy is configured in config/, never silent
data_standards.synthetic_only: Only synthetic or anonymised data may be committed
data_standards.reproducibility: Datasets generated by script with a recorded seed
data_standards.authorisation_tuple: (user_id, resource_id, permission) is authorised iff some role r exists with (user_id, r) in UA and (r, permission) in PA
data_standards.implementation_decision_note: How a permission relates to a resource (for example permissions carrying an action and optional resource scope) is an implementation decision to be reconciled with the report's data model in Milestone 2.

minimum: Every public function has at least one passing unit test
Every new module has a README and tests directory or test file
Every API endpoint has a contract test comparing the response with the Pydantic model
Every sample response validates against contracts.py
Edge cases: empty dataset, missing attributes, duplicate records, dangling references, single-class data
testing_requirements.reproducibility: Tests use fixed seeds and the small datasets in data_engineering/sample_datasets/
testing_requirements.ml_tests: Use tiny datasets so tests run in seconds on low-end laptops
testing_requirements.no_fabricated_results: Expected metric values in tests must come from independent calculation, never copied from model output

git_workflow.flow: feature branch -> pull request into develop -> review -> merge; develop -> main only for milestone releases
git_workflow.commit_convention: type(scope): summary, for example feat(policy_engine): add rule merger
pull_request_requirements: Touches only modules the author OWNS or is an approved CONTRIBUTOR for
Description lists changed modules and linked milestone
Docs updated if an interface changed
At least one reviewer other than the author
Module OWNER approval when the PR touches a module the author does not own
git_workflow.merge_approval: Integration owner (Jayed) merges into develop after reviews; Jayed's own PRs are reviewed and approved by another member
enforcement: GitHub branch protection on main and develop (require PR, require 1 approval, require status checks)
CODEOWNERS file maps paths to owners
CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml runs governance validation and tests
scripts/validate_governance.py checks JSON validity, ownership uniqueness and sample contracts

integration_rules: R1: Every member works only on assigned modules unless approved
R2: Nobody directly modifies another member's module
R3: Every module has a README
R4: Shared data structures follow approved schemas
R5: Frontend uses mock JSON until APIs are ready
R6: Backend API response structures never change without approval
R7: Every module includes unit tests
R8: All code is committed to GitHub
R9: No direct commits to main
R11: No confidential real employee data in the repository
R12: A module is not complete until its integration contract and tests pass

hard_rules.text: Every module has one clearly identified owner.
No member independently modifies another member's owned module.
All shared schemas must be approved before implementation.
Every module must provide a README.
All changes must pass review before merging.
No API response structure changes without approval.
No duplicate implementation of existing functionality.
No model training on the test set.
No unapproved ABAC rule is exported as an approved policy.
Never use a default ALLOW decision when policy evaluation fails. Fail safely (deny).
Never expose confidential datasets or credentials.

algorithm_constraints: Follow Appendix B of the project report; the report is authoritative
The Decision Tree is the rule extraction model
Random Forest and Gradient Boosting are accuracy references only; never extract rules from them as a replacement
Never evaluate the final policy only on the sampled negative dataset; report validation on the full access matrix
Keep the test set separate from training and hyperparameter selection
Avoid data leakage: fit encoders and imputers on training data only
Handle empty datasets and invalid attributes safely
Do not claim planned research results as achieved
security_requirements: Policy evaluation failures resolve to deny
Uploaded files are size-limited and parsed as data only; never executed
File names are sanitised; uploads stored under a generated dataset_id
No credentials, tokens or .env files committed
CORS limited to the configured frontend origin
Administrator approval is an explicit API call per rule decision; no auto-approve flag exists
prohibited_practices: Committing to main or develop directly
Editing another member's OWNED module without an approved change
Hardcoding sample data inside application logic
Training or tuning on the test split
Extracting final rules from Random Forest or Gradient Boosting
Committing trained model binaries, large datasets or real employee data
Claiming a feature works without running it

hardware_restrictions.low_spec_members: Shweta and Granthali work with small CSV/JSON files and lightweight Python; no model training on their machines
hardware_restrictions.frontend: Naeem develops against mock JSON and does not require the backend or trained models
hardware_restrictions.datasets: Small reproducible samples are committed; larger datasets are regenerated by script, not downloaded by everyone
hardware_restrictions.model_sharing: Trained models are not committed; Jayed shares result JSON that conforms to contracts

conflict_resolution.ownership_conflict: The module OWNER decides within 24 hours; if unresolved the four members vote and Jayed records the decision in docs/development_rules/DECISIONS.md
conflict_resolution.contract_conflict: Freeze work on the affected endpoint; propose a change request; all four members approve; bump CONTRACT_VERSION
conflict_resolution.requirement_conflict: The project report is authoritative. Where the report is silent, record an implementation decision in docs/development_rules/DECISIONS.md
conflict_resolution.ai_agent_conflict: Agents stop and report the conflict instead of choosing silently
